anchor.quote: Dealing whole rows cyclically into $W$ streams, where $W$ is the fixed number of streams
where $P$ is the number of prefix values
$R$ is the number of rows (here $R$ is a row count, not the scalar ring)
$B$ is the number of entries per row
the stream for each value $j$ of $b$ holds the entries $(a,j,c)$

gaps.quote: In item 4 the array is indexed by $[P]\times[R]\times[B]$
gaps.note: The page never says what [P], [R], [B] mean (the index set {0,...,P-1} etc.; paper defines [a]={0,...,a-1} at line 450), nor which digits of the address are the prefix, the row field and the suffix.

gaps.quote: merging the streams in any fixed order of the row classes
gaps.note: The page never says how rows are dealt cyclically (row r goes to stream r mod W, i.e. r=Wg+w), nor what the row classes are, nor that each stream then has shape [P]x[R/W]x[B]; item 4 is only cited and not explained.
